thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for dedicated-pool-us-west-2 (model: gpt-xxl-dedicated). Severity: P1 · paging oncall.

oncall-sre: paging in. saw alerts at ~11:12 UTC. p95 up ~2.3s -> p99 ~9s on streaming endpoints.
maria_g: customers reporting stalls for streaming sessions, some reconnects. CS says 3 enterprise customers seeing >30% error stream aborts.
kevin_h: checking allocator/queue depth. initial look: dedicated pool queue depth spiked to 1800 reqs, warmup success rate dropped. autoscaler logs show scale decisions delayed ~45s due to handshake timeouts.
ops-liaison: tagging impacted customers: AcmeCorp, FinSight, DocFlow. CS is drafting notifications.
eng-runtime: adding logs — handing over earliest traces. relevant keys: 
```
streaming_handler.go:HandleRequest: dispatch -> poolQueueLen=1823
autoscaler.go:Evaluate: desired=12 current=6 pending=3 lastHandshake=2026-02-11T11:11:40Z
warmup_manager.go:WarmupAttempt: failed=18/50 timeout=30s
```

oncall-sre: root cause hypothesis: dedicated pool saturated by burst traffic; autoscaler handshake to provision new slots is timing out because warmup landing pods aren't completing model KV load fast enough. leads to queue amplification and tail stalls.
maria_g: can we divert new traffic to hosted fallback pool for the three impacted customers? that's our standard mitigation.
eng-runtime: we can route by policy but need a fallthrough model variant that is compatibility-checked. for AcmeCorp they use pinned version v1.2.0 — fallback to v1.1.8 is possible but might regress quality.
kevin_h: quick mitigation path: 1) increase autoscaler aggressive target (manual bump desired to 18), 2) lower warmup parallelism to avoid thundering herd on NFS mount, 3) temporarily divert non-customer-critical traffic to hosted region-us-east.
oncall-sre: executing manual scale: `POST /internal/autoscaler/scale?pool=dedicated-pool-us-west-2&target=18` — kicked off. awaiting confirmation.
incident-bot: Autoscale action queued by oncall-sre. ETA provisioning ~65s.
eng-runtime: warmup logs show NFS cold reads for weights; we have serialized warmup causing long kv-cache loads. changing warmup to use prefetch threads might help. but it's a code change, not immediate.
ops-liaison: CS asks if we can throttle bursty non-authenticated traffic for a short window (rate-limit by ip) — that would reduce pressure.
maria_g: agree, do throttle for public playground/test keys. keep enterprise keys prioritized.
kevin_h: applied rate-limit rule to ingress for `playground-*` keys: `limit=50rps` — seen immediate drop in queue depth to ~900. p95 improved to ~1.2s, p99 to ~4.6s.
customer-success: Notifying AcmeCorp/FinSight/DocFlow of temporary mitigation and expected SLO impact.
oncall-sre: autoscaler finally provisioned 8 extra slots, some pods are warm but KV cache still warming. Observed streaming stalls decreasing but tail lingers.
eng-runtime: enabling progressive KV prefill flag on new nodes: `export PREFILL_KV=true` — this kicks background fetch to reduce first-token stalls. applied to new nodes only.
kevin_h: after prefill flag, p99 dropped to ~1.9s over 5m, streaming stalls down to 2%. significant improvement.
maria_g: CS reports two customers still seeing intermittent reconnects (~<5% sessions). root cause lingering coldkeys on older nodes.
oncall-sre: plan next 30m: a) keep manual scale until autoscaler learns new thresholds, b) cordon old nodes with highest cold-hit ratio and spin replacement warm nodes, c) follow up with eng-runtime for warmup tuning.
eng-runtime: agreed. creating follow-up ticket: WARMUP-1729 for async prefetch + reduce per-node serial warmup.
ops-liaison: oncall handover in 2 hours — i'll add notes to the incident channel and tag next rotation.
devex-bot: Added runbook snippet: 
```
If dedicated pool p99 > 5s and queue depth > 1000:
  - Page oncall SRE
  - Manual scale to desired=2x current up to pool cap
  - Throttle non-enterprise keys
  - Enable PREFILL_KV on new nodes
  - Cordon cold nodes for replacement
```
maria_g: customer impact summary for status page (short): "We experienced elevated latency and intermittent streaming session interruptions affecting a subset of customers on dedicated-us-west-2 between 11:12–11:45 UTC. We have provisioned additional capacity and mitigations; engineers continue to monitor. Root cause: warmup/handshake delays with autoscaler under burst"
kevin_h: telemetry note: autoscaler handshake timeouts peaked at 47s; need follow-up to harden handshake and possibly reduce required warmup barrier. filing postmortem.
oncall-sre: ok folks — we'll keep monitoring for one more cycle. if p99 stable <2.5s for 15m, start de-escalation and remove rate-limits.
eng-runtime: also recommending a short-term config change: reduce `required_warmup_success_rate` from 0.9 to 0.6 for burst-surge policy to avoid blocking scale. will propose as opt-in for Dedicated until warmup refactor.
customer-success: CS will update customers in 30 minutes with mitigation details and ETA for full resolution.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. severity degraded to P2.
oncall-sre: handoff: @next-oncall you are on deck. logs and runbook in #incidents pinned. any questions ping me. :thumbsup:
kevin_h: follow-ups: (1) postmortem with timeline and metrics, (2) warmup perf ticket, (3) autoscaler handshake retry/backoff tuning.
maria_g: noted. i'll draft postmortem and link customer comms.
eng-runtime: leaving traces and heap/procstats in the ticket.
devex-bot: Reminder: add checklists for fallback-route tests in integration suites.
oncall-sre: closing thread, continuing watch.
